title: Assadi's 'Paradiso 17' wins National Book Award for fiction; Rushdie gets lifetime medal
dek: Rahul Bery's translation of Vicente Luis Mora's 'Centroeuropa' takes the translated literature prize at the 77th awards in New York.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Hannah Lillith Assadi's 'Paradiso 17' won the fiction prize at the 77th National Book Awards in New York on Wednesday night, and Salman Rushdie, the Mumbai-born novelist, received the National Book Foundation's medal for lifetime achievement.

The other winners were Abdelrahman ElGendy's 'Huna: A Memoir of Revolution, Prison, and Becoming' in nonfiction, Brenda Hillman's 'Still House in the Desert: An eco-contemplation' in poetry, and 'The Fight of Our Lives: AIDS in America' by David Levithan and Gabriel Duckels in young people's literature. The translated literature prize went to 'Centroeuropa' by the Spanish writer Vicente Luis Mora, translated from Spanish by Rahul Bery. Each winner receives $10,000 and a bronze sculpture, and each finalist $1,000.

Rushdie is the 39th recipient of the Medal for Distinguished Contribution to American Letters, which the foundation has given since 1988. When it announced the award in September, the foundation called him "a bold, innovative writer and an indefatigable defender of free speech". Rushdie, whose 'Midnight's Children' won the Booker Prize in 1981, survived a stabbing at a lecture in Chautauqua, New York, in 2022 and wrote about it in his memoir 'Knife', a National Book Award nonfiction finalist.

The foundation's Literarian Award, for service to the literary community, went to the paediatrician and author Perri Klass, national medical director of the early-literacy programme Reach Out and Read.

The awards, run by the non-profit National Book Foundation, are among the most prominent literary prizes in the United States.
